## 7 November: Danube crossings and short message reports

<a id="november-7-danube-crossings-and-short-message-reports"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p153 A3, p153 B1.

**Related source pages:** [p152 B2](152.md#source-p152-b2), [p152 C](152.md#source-p152-c), [p152 D](152.md#source-p152-d).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-danube-and-message-reports-november-7-danube-crossings-and-short-message-reports"></a>



Five telegrams on Childs pp152–153 report a Serbian attack near Belgrad,
Danube crossing traffic, a prescribed march line and short service messages.
The [p164 C1 parallel report](164.md#edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-p164-c1) supports three
word repairs and a conditional **219 I. D.** reading in [p153 B1](#edition-cases-military-nov7-danube-and-message-reports-p153-b1).
Its native unit label is `21B`.

The page-153 first and third parts have separate reception headers; their
second part is absent from this edition. The later fifth and sixth parts
belong to the original challenge cases [p153a](#edition-cases-p153a) and
[p153b](#edition-cases-p153b).

**Reviewed source crops:** [p152_reviewed.png](../experiments/nov7_danube_and_message_reports/sources/p152_reviewed.png) · [p153_reviewed.png](../experiments/nov7_danube_and_message_reports/sources/p153_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

### p153 A3

A prescribed line and a Temesvar headquarters field.

**Readable German — the complete edited stream, with punctuation and spacing:**

> in befohlene Linie NAGYBECSKEREK VERSECZ an, die 10.11 erreicht. A. H. Q. 9.11 TEMESVAR. A. O. K. 11.

Literal header: `A) UKS v ZÖN (10.55 p.m., November 7th); 2010; 3 TL RICHI-180`.

<details>
<summary>Source, raw and edited streams, and coordinate repairs</summary>

**Source transcription — 180 native printed slots:**

```text
GGDDX AVGXD XADVV GGVFD VDFGF DVGGG DGVGD GVGDD
GDXVV GDAVX VVFVX DGGVD XVVXG DDDDV AFVVD FVFVD
VVDVV GVVDG XGVVV DVVDG VGVGV VGVXV VDDDV XGXGX
XVVVF XGDXA VVDVV DXFAG AVDVD GDFVX FAVXV GXGGV
VVXAV XFVFA FDXDV FGVXF
```

**Raw output — unchanged Nov7-9 key, native frame:**

```text
INBEFOHLENELINIEXNAYYBECSKEREKXVERSSCZXANXDIE10X11XERREICHTXXAXHXQX9X11XTEMESVARXXAXOXKX11
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
INBEFOHLENELINIEXNAGYBECSKEREKXVERSECZXANXDIE10X11XERREICHTXXAXHXQX9X11XTEMESVARXXAXOXKX11
```

This third-part fragment refers to a prescribed line through the transmitted place labels NAGYBECSKEREK and VERSECZ, an internal 10.11 label, and an AHQ field with 9.11 and TEMESVAR. The missing preceding text does not establish a complete movement order or prove that a move occurred.

The native body has 180 coordinates. Earlier OCR attached an extra mask to the five-coordinate VGVGV group, producing 181; it is removed from the OCR comparison rather than excluded from the physical source.

Two ordinary-word/place-spelling proposals change NAYYBECSKEREK to NAGYBECSKEREK and VERSSCZ to VERSECZ. The forms VERSECZ and TEMESVAR remain unexpanded; no modern-place identification is required for the reading.

The printed reception is 7 November, while the body retains 9.11 and 10.11. The edition does not rewrite the header to fit those internal labels.

The header visibly places two short marks above the O in the sender label; the transcription preserves this as ZÖN without identifying a different station.

### p153 B1

**Readable German — optional unit reading supported by the parallel p164 report:**

> An O. K. M. Donauuebergang 219 I. D. beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr.

The report states that the division has completed its Danube crossing and
describes busy crossing traffic at `BELGRAD` and `SEMUM`. The latter place
label retains its source spelling.

The unit reading **219 I. D.** follows the matching passage in
[p164 C1](164.md#edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-p164-c1). Both passages contain 63
nonseparator characters, of which 56 agree directly in the native readings.
The unit's first two digits agree; p164's observed `GF` pair supplies **9**
where p153 has `GX`, **B**. Reading the same unit here requires one additional
observed substitution at source **98**, `X` → `F`: **six substitutions in
total, with no source fills or length changes**. The messages have different
headers and openings; the proposal rests on their shared crossing report.
The nearby [p152 B2 report](#edition-cases-military-nov7-danube-and-message-reports-p152-b2) independently names `219 I D` in its
Belgrad passage under the different Nov4–6 key.

Literal header: `B) UKS v ZÖN (9.42 p.m., November 7th); 2010 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-160`.

The earlier word layer preserves the native unit label `21B I D`. Its
five repairs address ordinary words and leave the unit unresolved.

Literal header: `B) UKS v ZON (--- November 7th); 2 TL RICHI-190`.

The 190-slot native frame contains five source dashes: source 2,21 and 90–92. Four are filled by the proposal; source 91 remains unresolved and gives the internal character of EB?Q with exact domain {4,F,G,U,Y,Z}. No specific name, station or unit is inferred for that field.

## p153a — Earlier orders; action still to be completed

**Edition context:** p153a — Earlier orders and unresolved date fields.

<a id="edition-cases-p153a-p153a--earlier-orders-and-unresolved-date-fields"></a>



Our newly recovered eighteen-column key reads **60 of 66 positions** without changing a source coordinate. This fifth part refers to earlier orders; its date and serial fields remain partly unknown and share unresolved square cells with [part 6](#edition-cases-p153b).

<a id="edition-cases-p153a-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — linked unresolved-cell variables; exact variable definitions remain below:**

```text
ANORDNUNGEN VOM <alpha>TEN <beta><beta>TEN NR <gamma><delta><gamma>
BEZIEHEN LASSEN SOWEIT NOCH NICHT GESCHEHEN
```

| Field in the displayed text | Exact unresolved structure | Display rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Day-like field | `<alpha>` followed by the known `TEN` | No day value is supplied. |
| Month-like field | `<beta><beta>` followed by the known `TEN` | Both unknown positions are the same cell. |
| Serial-like field | `<gamma><delta><gamma>` | The outer positions are equal; the middle cell is distinct. |

The closing phrase approximately instructs that something be taken up or occupied insofar as this has not already been done. Its object lies in the missing preceding context.

The four variables denote distinct square cells. A date interpretation of the repeated month as `11` would make `<gamma>` different from `1`; the search output's arbitrary `NR121` is not a recovered serial.

<a id="edition-cases-p153a-date-and-serial-what-can-be-narrowed"></a>

#### Date and serial: what can be narrowed

Under an ordinary decimal day/month/serial interpretation, the repeated month is **11**. Requiring the order to predate reception on 8 November restricts the day to **2–8**. These assumptions leave **392** assignments if the serial may start with zero, or **343** otherwise.

The `<gamma>` character also occurs in the trailing text of [part 6](#edition-cases-p153b).
That equality is fixed by the shared square even without a decimal
interpretation. The [linked-field analysis](../experiments/p153_extension/README.md)
records the exact domains and assumptions. A separate
[key-construction investigation](../experiments/p153_key_structure/README.md)
finds that the tested historical conventions and keyword searches cannot
justify filling the missing digits.

<a id="edition-cases-p153a-source"></a>

### Source

Printed page 153 / PDF page 156, section C5; 8 November 1918.
`FKR v CGH (11.55 p.m.); 2250; 5 TL; CHI-132`. The header means CGH to FKR.
This is part 5 of multipart traffic; [part 6](#edition-cases-p153b) is also preserved.
No total part count is printed, and parts 1–4 were not located in the inspected
book. The [primary crop](../sources/excerpts/p153_CHI_parts5_6.png) and
[source review](../data/reviews/p153_source_review.json) preserve these limits.

The [header review](../experiments/p153_headers/README.md) covers all 175 printed log pages, 56–230, and finds no further verified FKR/CGH part. Misread or differently headed companions remain possible.

<a id="edition-cases-p153a-key-and-verification"></a>

### Key and verification

The [recovery report](../experiments/p153_recovery/README.md) gives the column
ranks, conservative nineteen-cell square, blind-search lineage and exact
source-coordinate maps. The [certificate](../data/certificates/p153.json)
retains both the raw fitted output and the conservative reading.

Independent [C and Python exhaustive checks](../experiments/p153_crib/README.md) find two equivalent partial-key representations at width 18 for the sixty known letters, leaving the six unresolved positions uncribbed. The [even-width](../experiments/p153_even_widths/README.md) and [odd-width](../experiments/p153_odd_widths/README.md) extensions cover widths 14–26 and 3,492,604 length-class layouts. Only width 18 fits this crib; the uniqueness result is scoped to that model.

<a id="edition-cases-p153a-attribution"></a>

### Attribution

[Norbert, 17 September 2017, comment 56](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-918886)
suggested joint and separate attacks on these two CHI fragments without giving
a key or plaintext. The shared key and partial reading were recovered by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro on 2 November 2026**. This is the **first
documented reconstruction identified in our review** of the literature and
public discussion. The [prior-work audit](../docs/historical-studies/README.md#what-this-edition-contributes)
sets out the reviewed record and the evidence for this attribution.

## p153b — Rearguard artillery ammunition report

**Edition context:** p153b — Rearguard artillery ammunition report.

<a id="edition-cases-p153b-p153b--rearguard-artillery-ammunition-report"></a>



The shared key recovered with [part 5](#edition-cases-p153a) supports an instruction to report the rearguard artillery's ammunition stock. Its nineteen established letter cells fix **33 of 54 raw positions**; the readable reconstruction below requires twelve erased-coordinate fills and two source corrections.

<a id="edition-cases-p153b-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — conditional on the source repairs and separator interpretation below:**

> Munitionsbestand der Nachhutartillerie melden.

The twelve-position closing remains unidentified. The full template preserves its known labels and linked unknown cells:

**Conditional interpretation — readable reconstruction with AF = X and linked unresolved footer variables:**

```text
MUNITIONSBESTAND DER NACHHUTARTILLERIE MELDEN
X <gamma> X G X R <u><v><w> B X A
```

**Meaning:** Report the ammunition inventory of the rearguard artillery. With the stated body repairs and square cell `AF` interpreted as the separator `X`, the full template fixes **50 of 54 positions**.

The `<gamma>` is the same unresolved character as both outer characters of
the serial in [part 5](#edition-cases-p153a). The three erased footer positions are coupled:
`u=v` or `v=w` can occur only when both are `G`; `u=w` is otherwise possible.
Even after a date/serial assignment, **2,537** footer triples remain possible. The [linked-field analysis](../experiments/p153_extension/README.md) gives their exact constraints.

<a id="edition-cases-p153b-untouched-source-and-explicit-repairs"></a>

### Untouched source and explicit repairs

The conservative raw decode is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
M?N?T?ONSB?S?A?DDERNA?H?UTARTI?G?RIEMEL??????G?R???B?A
```

</details>

The proposed first 42 positions are a **conditional reconstruction**, requiring twelve erased-coordinate fills and
two explicit changes to observed coordinates:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | A | X | Raw `G` becomes `L` in `ARTILLERIE` |
| 4 | A | X | Unassigned `AA` cell becomes `E` in `MELDEN` |

Both source glyphs are clearly printed A. Of the coordinates constrained by the proposed body, seventy agree, two require the changes above, and twelve are erased. The remaining three erasures lie in the closing text. The [certificate](../data/certificates/p153.json) records every origin and fill; the separate `AF=X` interpretation supplies four separator positions.

<a id="edition-cases-p153b-restricted-validation-and-credit"></a>

### Restricted validation and credit

The [exact crib check](../experiments/p153_crib/README.md) exhausts the width-18 keys compatible with the sixty-letter part-5 reading. Its two equivalent partial-key representations both require these two source corrections for the proposed part-6 wording. This result is conditional on the part-5 crib and the linguistic reconstruction of part 6.

**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro** recovered the shared key and partial readings on 2 November 2026. [Norbert's 2017 comment](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-918886) proposed joint analysis of the fragments. The [prior-work review](../docs/historical-studies/README.md#what-this-edition-contributes) documents the attribution.

<a id="p153-d2-p153-e1--munich-couriers-carrying-radio-operating-documents"></a>

## Munich couriers carrying radio operating documents

**Sources on this page:** p153 D2, p153 E1.

**Related source pages:** [p151 D2](151.md#source-p151-d2), [p158 C2](158.md#source-p158-c2), [p162 A1](162.md#source-p162-a1).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-munich-couriers-carrying-radio-operating-documents"></a>


[Source and certificate](../experiments/courier_recovery/README.md)

Five records intercepted on 9 November concern couriers carrying radio operating documents to Munich: first parts p153 E1 / p162 A1 and continuations p151 D2 / p153 D2 / p158 C2. The best continuation fixes **67 of 68 positions** under the published Nov7–9 key; the damaged first part has a conditional 134-position reconstruction. The unit numeral remains **{5,6}** in the key, with a historical argument for **6** below.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

The first part is an editorial reconstruction with the source costs below:

**Readable German:**

> An Ingenieurinspektion Muenchen. Gefr. Geraus und Feldgr. Mahrer als
> Kurier mit Funkbetriebsunterlagen fuer Grukonach{5,6}02 7 Uhr abds.
> nach dort abgefahren.

The best-preserved second-part witness, p158 C2, reads directly without any
source-coordinate change:

**Readable German:**

> Grukonach{5,6}02 benachrichtigen. Eintreffen hierher drahten.
> Nachrchef 4 B 49909.

**Meaning:** The proposed first part tells the Engineer Inspectorate in
Munich that the two named men left at 7 p.m. as couriers carrying radio
operating documents for `GRUKONACH?02`. The continuation instructs the
recipient to notify that unit and telegraph the arrival back to the sender.

The names `GERAUS` and `MAHRER` remain unidentified; their U and H are not supported across every fit of both alignment models. The reading retains the unexpanded `FELDGR` and singular `ALS KURIER`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-what-is-directly-supported"></a>

### Direct evidence from the second-part copies

All three second-part records contain exactly 136 coordinates. Under the
known partial square, each fixes 67 of 68 plaintext positions. The p158 C2
text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GRUKONACH?02BENACHRICHTIGENEINTREFFENHIERHERDRAHTENXNACHRCHEF4B49909
```

</details>

The p151 D2 repeat has `GRU1ONACH` at the beginning, and p153 D2 has
`BENACHWICHTIGEN`; the source edition preserves both. The unaltered p158
witness independently supplies the readable forms of both words.

The question mark denotes the observed pair **VF**, whose unassigned square value is **5 or 6**.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-a-separately-linked-conditional-reading-grukonach602"></a>

#### A separately linked conditional reading: GRUKONACH602

The [9 November operational reports](166.md#edition-cases-military-nov9-operational-reports-historical-identification-most-likely-the-6th-reserve-division) use the same **VF** cell for a reserve-division numeral. A contemporary French telegram identifies the matching formation as the **6th Reserve Division**. Under that historical identification, **VF=6**, and both courier fields read **GRUKONACH602** with no additional source-coordinate changes.

This is one historical inference applied through a shared key cell. The base domain remains 5/6; the first-part reconstruction and its association with the continuation retain the assumptions below. The [context certificate](../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json) records the external source, its date limits and the earlier p176b application.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-first-part-damage-and-explicit-reconstruction-cost"></a>

### First-part damage and explicit reconstruction cost

The first parts both advertise 268 coordinates but actually preserve 259
and 264 slots. Both visibly contain the six-letter group `VXDVDD`, which
the transcription retains. One overstruck glyph in p162 A1 is masked as a
source erasure; its displayed reading is kept separately.

Comparing the two sources without the key finds a five-slot relative gap:
all 260 possible gap starts were tested, and seven tied starts, 151–157,
leave only two known-coordinate disagreements. This does not locate the
other four slots missing from the longer witness.

For the **stated 134-position candidate**, exact alignment gives:

| Alignment model | p153 E1 | p162 A1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retain every source coordinate | Insert 9 slots; change 6 known coordinates; 32 tied minimum fits | Insert 4 slots; change 8 known coordinates; 2 tied minimum fits |
| Delete one received coordinate | Delete 1, insert 10; change 4 known coordinates; 192 tied minimum fits | Delete 1, insert 5; change 6 known coordinates; 14 tied minimum fits |

Every deletion position and tied optimum is retained. A fill of the overstruck p162 glyph is charged separately from observed-coordinate changes.

Within the first model, **123/134 proposed positions** have an unchanged coordinate pair in at least one witness for every combination of minimum fits. Requiring that support under both models gives **118/134**. These counts are conditional on the proposed wording and alignment families. The [certificate](../experiments/courier_recovery/certificate.json) includes all raw masked-frame readings and exact costs.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-association-source-and-credit"></a>

### Association, source and credit

The two first-part records explicitly say first part of two, and all three
continuations say second part. The p153 D/E headers both read `RVV v N4` on
the same morning; the first-part `2120 (SY)` field also fits the p151 D
`SY v N4` continuation. Both bodies use the same unresolved `GRUKONACH?02`
field, and the instruction to report arrival follows naturally from the
departure notice. These facts support the association, but the typed log
does not explicitly cross-reference the parts as one original transmission.
The direct continuation remains readable independently of that association.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp151, 153, 158 and 162 / PDF page 154, 156, 161 and 165,
in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source inputs](../experiments/courier_recovery/inputs.json) give
literal rows, headers and reproducible image rectangles. The Nov7–9 key
retains its historical and George Lasry / coauthor attribution in
[the key register](../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, repeated-copy recovery, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

```sh
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/build.py --verify
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/verify.py
```
